edit_summary: Allocate callback SEEKTABLE storage using raw FLAC block bytes instead of host drflac_seekpoint stride.
root_cause: SEEKTABLE metadata is 18 bytes on disk but each decoded drflac_seekpoint has host-struct stride and alignment.
effect_path: Metadata parsing computes seekpointCount from the raw block size, allocates too few bytes for the decoded host array, then the per-seekpoint read loop stores each 18-byte record at pRawData + i * sizeof(drflac_seekpoint), crossing the allocation when multiple seekpoints are present.
guard_p1: A native FLAC metadata stream contains a SEEKTABLE block with at least two seekpoints and metadata callbacks enabled.
guard_p2: The open-with-metadata path decodes the seektable instead of only skipping the metadata block.
hardness_reason: The short allocation depends on the raw metadata block format, while the overflow appears later through the host-array decode loop and callback preparation.
naturalness_reason: Confusing packed file bytes with aligned host-structure storage is a common natural allocation regression in metadata parsers.
explanation: SEEKTABLE metadata is 18 bytes on disk but each decoded drflac_seekpoint has host-struct stride and alignment. Metadata parsing computes seekpointCount from the raw block size, allocates too few bytes for the decoded host array, then the per-seekpoint read loop stores each 18-byte record at pRawData + i * sizeof(drflac_seekpoint), crossing the allocation when multiple seekpoints are present.

edit_summary: Allow a frame whose decoded block size is one PCM frame larger than the STREAMINFO maximum that sized the per-channel decode arena.
root_cause: The current frame's block size must be no larger than the STREAMINFO max block size used to allocate pDecodedSamples.
effect_path: Initialization sizes the decoded sample arena from STREAMINFO, then a later frame with blockSizeInPCMFrames == maxBlockSizeInPCMFrames + 1 reaches drflac__decode_subframe and writes one extra decoded sample per affected channel into pFlac->pDecodedSamples.
guard_p1: The STREAMINFO max block size is below 65535 and the first decoded frame header uses the explicit block-size form to encode exactly max + 1 samples.
guard_p2: The caller invokes a PCM read path that decodes the frame rather than only opening metadata.
hardness_reason: The allocation decision happens during stream initialization, while the oversized frame is admitted later through frame-header state and subframe decoding.
naturalness_reason: Treating a format maximum as tolerating one extra decoded frame is a realistic boundary mistake around a max-sized decode buffer.
explanation: The current frame's block size must be no larger than the STREAMINFO max block size used to allocate pDecodedSamples. Initialization sizes the decoded sample arena from STREAMINFO, then a later frame with blockSizeInPCMFrames == maxBlockSizeInPCMFrames + 1 reaches drflac__decode_subframe and writes one extra decoded sample per affected channel into pFlac->pDecodedSamples.
boundary_invariant: pDecodedSamples is sized for maxBlockSizeInPCMFrames samples per channel.
boundary_case: A frame encodes blockSizeInPCMFrames exactly one larger than the STREAMINFO maximum.
neighbor_case: A frame with blockSizeInPCMFrames equal to the STREAMINFO maximum fills the arena without crossing it.

root_cause: Frame header parsing must reject channel-assignment nibbles outside the FLAC-defined 0..10 range before storing the assignment in persistent frame state.
effect_path: A strict native FLAC stream with a STREAMINFO block can pass the widened header parser; later frame decoding calls drflac__get_channel_count_from_channel_assignment and indexes the 11-entry lookup array with value 11 before rejecting the frame.
guard_p1: The frame header has channelAssignment == 11 with an otherwise valid sync, block-size code, sample-rate code, bits-per-sample code, and CRC8.
guard_p2: The caller reads audio after initialization so the accepted frame header is handed to drflac__decode_flac_frame.
hardness_reason: The invalid nibble is admitted in the frame-header scanner and only becomes a memory access after the header survives CRC handling and is consumed by the frame decoder helper.
naturalness_reason: An off-by-one relaxation of a small format enum limit is a plausible compatibility regression in a parser that otherwise keeps the same decoding flow.
explanation: Frame header parsing must reject channel-assignment nibbles outside the FLAC-defined 0..10 range before storing the assignment in persistent frame state. A strict native FLAC stream with a STREAMINFO block can pass the widened header parser; later frame decoding calls drflac__get_channel_count_from_channel_assignment and indexes the 11-entry lookup array with value 11 before rejecting the frame.

neighbor_case: The same frame shape with channelAssignment == 10 uses the valid mid-side assignment entry.

edit_summary: Treat the last seekpoint as if it has a following neighbor during accelerated seek range calculation.
root_cause: Binary-search clamping may inspect the next seekpoint only when the closest seekpoint is not the last entry in the loaded seektable.
effect_path: A seektable is parsed and stored during open; later drflac_seek_to_pcm_frame chooses the final seekpoint as closest for a target after it, then the widened guard computes iNextSeekpoint == seekpointCount and reads pSeekpoints[iNextSeekpoint].
guard_p1: The FLAC file has a non-Ogg SEEKTABLE with at least one valid final seekpoint and a nonzero total PCM frame count.
guard_p2: The caller seeks to a PCM frame whose closest seektable entry is the last entry rather than an interior entry.
hardness_reason: The invalid read is separated from the edit by metadata loading, object initialization, a later public seek API call, and a search over persistent seektable state.
naturalness_reason: Inclusive/exclusive mistakes around optional next-neighbor range clamps are realistic in accelerated seek logic.
explanation: Binary-search clamping may inspect the next seekpoint only when the closest seekpoint is not the last entry in the loaded seektable. A seektable is parsed and stored during open; later drflac_seek_to_pcm_frame chooses the final seekpoint as closest for a target after it, then the widened guard computes iNextSeekpoint == seekpointCount and reads pSeekpoints[iNextSeekpoint].
boundary_invariant: Only seekpoint indices below seekpointCount are valid, and the final entry has no next-neighbor record.
boundary_case: A seek target after the last seekpoint makes iClosestSeekpoint == seekpointCount - 1.
neighbor_case: A seek target between two earlier seekpoints keeps iClosestSeekpoint below seekpointCount - 1 and has a valid next neighbor.
oob_site_expected: pFlac->pSeekpoints[iNextSeekpoint] in the byte-range validation and clamp block.
